Nausea — hypothesis to test: peppermint tea temperature. Warm liquids promote gastric emptying + gentle smooth-muscle relaxation; cold liquids slow emptying and can trigger mild spasm in a reactive stomach, so the same tea may soothe hot and irritate cold. Peppermint-specific: menthol is an antispasmodic (helps IBS-type lower-gut symptoms) but relaxes the lower esophageal sphincter, which can worsen reflux. Warm tea clears the stomach faster, so less time for the LES effect; a cold drink lingers, giving more downside and less benefit. TEST: note WHERE the cool version hurts — burning/pressure behind the sternum = LES/reflux effect (peppermint may be a mixed bag at any temperature); lower cramping or unease = temperature effect (stick with hot).

RETROSPECTIVE — re: the January 2025–August 2025 episode (couldn't sleep ~5 days in a row while crying constantly). Reframing what that actually was: Nobody goes 5 days in a row on near-zero sleep from pure depression. The body physically can't — depression makes you tired, and tired bodies eventually crash and sleep. Going 5 straight days without that collapse is the tell-tale sign of manic activation — sleep NEED dropped, not just sleep ability. That's a different engine entirely. Put it together: crying all the time (the depressive emotional content) running on top of 5 days of not needing sleep (the manic activation) = the textbook picture of a MIXED STATE, not plain depression — the high-energy engine and the low mood running at the same time. Worth telling my psychiatrist: '5 days without sleeping while crying constantly' — that one sentence points to mixed/bipolar features, which is treated differently from unipolar depression (some antidepressants can worsen mixed states).

🔑 BIGGEST CLUE (eating helps OR hurts depending on my stomach state) — MY OWN WORDS: "When I'm in the middle of a stomach-induced panic attack — what I now think is an ACID-REFLUX panic — eating does NOT help. I feel instantly more nauseous, even after I've taken Xanax. But when I haven't eaten much and I'm faint and panicky, running on empty, then eating DOES help."

CLINICAL READ: These look like two opposite body states wearing the same "panic" mask. State A is a FULL, sour, refluxy stomach where my vagus nerve (gut-brain wire) is already firing — adding food stretches it more and pushes acid up, so nausea spikes; Xanax can't touch that because it calms my brain, not my stomach. State B is an EMPTY, hollow, faint state from going too long without food plus over-breathing — a small bland bite settles it. Same action (eating), opposite result, because the starting stomach state is opposite. SELF-TEST: sour/full/just-ate -> don't eat, treat as reflux (upright, ginger tea/water, in-4/out-6-8, wait). Hollow/faint/3-4h empty AND danger-screen clear -> eat 2-3 bites of a safe food, then STOP and recheck; if worse, it was reflux.
